tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrap copied sources, preserved UWP csproj under .uwp-source, and mass-rewrote Windows.UI.Xaml->Microsoft.UI.Xaml; build reached a near-clean state quickly.
session-log.txt:3379-3380 '[PASS] dotnet build succeeded (56 warning(s), 0 WUI analyzer warning(s))' confirmed a clean build.
session-log.txt:2375 native dotnet build used throughout (no BuildAndRun wrapper); surfaced the real compiler errors.

tools_problematic.problem: Only rewrites Windows.UI.Xaml; leaves the non-Xaml Windows.UI helper classes (Colors/ColorHelper) that also moved to Microsoft.UI, so they surface later as build errors.
tools_problematic.evidence: session-log.txt:2806-2813 CS0234/CS0103 for 'Colors' after bootstrap ran.

tool_limitations.limitation: Bulk rewrite regex 'Windows\.UI\.Xaml' does not cover fully-qualified Windows.UI.Colors / Windows.UI.ColorHelper usages.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add drop-in-safe -replace passes for Windows.UI.Colors and Windows.UI.ColorHelper, with a trailing boundary so the Windows.UI.Color struct is left alone.

special_apis.special_handling: Classes moved to Microsoft.UI; the Windows.UI.Color STRUCT stayed in Windows.UI. Do not rewrite 'using Windows.UI;' wholesale.
Unchanged WinRT API; works as-is in WinUI 3. Hardware-gated: with no lamp present, acquisition returns null and the toggle stays disabled (faithful to UWP).

errors_encountered.error: CS0234: The type or namespace name 'Colors' does not exist in the namespace 'Windows.UI'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Bootstrap rewrote only Windows.UI.Xaml; the fully-qualified Windows.UI.Colors.Green/Red references in MainPage.xaml.cs were left pointing at the old namespace where the Colors class no longer lives in WinUI 3.
errors_encountered.fix: Retarget Windows.UI.Colors -> Microsoft.UI.Colors (add 'using Microsoft.UI;' or fully-qualify).

errors_encountered.error: CS0103: The name 'Colors' does not exist in the current context
errors_encountered.root_cause: Scenario2 used 'using Windows.UI;' then unqualified Colors.Blue; after migration the named-color class is Microsoft.UI.Colors, so the unqualified name no longer resolves.
errors_encountered.fix: Change the directive to 'using Microsoft.UI;' (or add it) so unqualified Colors resolves.

errors_encountered.error: XamlCompiler WMC0909/WMC1111: Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario / DataTemplates containing x:Bind need x:DataType
errors_encountered.root_cause: Self-inflicted: the migrated MainPage.xaml used {x:Bind Title} with x:DataType=local:Scenario, but the ORIGINAL UWP used a plain {Binding Title} DataTemplate. The unnecessary x:Bind failed to resolve the type at MarkupCompilePass.
errors_encountered.fix: Reverted the DataTemplate to plain {Binding Title}, matching the original UWP.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: 6-error build failure (CS0234 x2, CS0103) after the first full build
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Bootstrap namespace rewrite did not cover Windows.UI.Colors/ColorHelper, which are non-Xaml helper classes that also relocated to Microsoft.UI.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Manually retargeted Windows.UI.Colors -> Microsoft.UI.Colors and switched 'using Windows.UI;' to 'using Microsoft.UI;'.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Extending Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 to auto-rewrite Windows.UI.Colors/ColorHelper, and a MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md note clarifying the class-moved / struct-stayed distinction.

dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Agent introduced x:Bind + x:DataType that the original UWP did not use.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Reverted to plain {Binding Title} as in the original.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: No skill change — a faithful copy of the original UWP DataTemplate avoids it (dev-agent slip).
